pitch: Why some leaders and organizations inspire lastingly: the golden circle, trust and consistency.
br: three circles · start at the center
challenging the status quo · products come second
clear why · disciplined how · aligned what
The law of diffusion of innovations
The Wright brothers and the dream
growth · the what takes over · forgetting
quiz: In what order do inspiring leaders communicate?
They start from the center of the golden circle: their belief, then how they do things, then their products.
Why is “making money” not a why?
Because it is a result, not a belief
The why is a belief that goes beyond financial results.
Manipulation produces transactions; inspiration produces loyalty
Price, promotions and fear work in the short term but create no lasting attachment.
What is the difference between repeat business and loyalty?
Repeat business comes from convenience or price; loyalty resists even a better offer
A loyal customer stays when a competitor is cheaper; a repeat customer leaves.
Why does Sinek recommend writing values as verbs?
Because an action can be checked, while a noun stays abstract
“Always do the right thing” can be checked; “integrity” remains a word.
According to the law of diffusion of innovations, who should you convince first?
Mass success begins with a convinced minority that then carries the majority.
Checking that a decision is consistent with the why
The why acts as a filter for sorting opportunities and advice.
What should you keep in mind about the biological explanation of the golden circle?
It is very simplified; only the idea that decisions are not purely rational is solid
A clean split between the emotional and rational brain does not match current neuroscience.
